01 / Before you start

Check your disc dump.

Shinka currently targets the European multilingual release, Digimon World 2003, disc ID SLES-03936. The US Digimon World 3 and Japanese releases are not supported by this build.

For the current setup, keep the .cue file and its matching .bin file together. The CUE describes the disc; the BIN contains its data. Select the BIN when building and the CUE when launching.

Choose English in the game for Shinka's expanded menus. An ISO, CHD or multi-BIN dump is not a supported input to this build guide; renaming its extension will not convert it.

A folder with both files

My disc dump/
  game.cue
  game.bin

Your filenames can be different. Keep the name inside the CUE matched to the BIN it references.

How is the version checked?

The build verifies the entire BIN before preparing game code. The currently supported SHA-1 is:

457cb233349ba841e03b33d8060f8fbcadd45cb3

A different hash is rejected. Even the right title or region alone does not guarantee a match.

02 / Current setup

Build once. Then launch.

This is the developer route available today. If you want setup without terminals or build tools, wait for the installer; it isn't ready yet.

  1. Install the build tools

    You need Visual Studio 2022 with Desktop development with C++ and a Windows SDK, CMake 3.20 or newer, Git, and Python 3.11 or newer. Open Developer PowerShell for VS 2022. Git, CMake and Python must be available there. The first build also needs internet access to download dependencies.

  2. Get the source

    In a local development folder, run:

    git clone https://github.com/JohnnySn0w/dmw2003-shinka.git
cd dmw2003-shinka
git clone https://github.com/Alexbeav/digimon-world-2003-recomp.git ../audit-recomp
git -C ../audit-recomp checkout 6ae36f9564b0c81b64428aa5355375d945d56d53
git -C ../audit-recomp submodule update --init psxrecomp

  3. Build using your BIN

    Replace the example path with your own BIN's full path. Keep the quotes. Leave the terminal open until the build and its checks finish successfully.

    ./tools/build_windows.ps1 -DiscBin 'C:\Games\My disc dump\game.bin' -CandidateRoot ../audit-recomp -Jobs 2

    The original disc file is read, not patched. Generated game files stay local. Two build jobs limit compile concurrency on a busy computer.

  4. Launch using your CUE

    From the same Shinka folder, run:

    ./tools/launch_windows.ps1 -DiscCue 'C:\Games\My disc dump\game.cue' -EvolutionJournal -SaveDirectory 'output/player-saves'

    This enables DIGIVOLUTIONS and SETTINGS. It does not turn on boosted EXP or alternate music. Close the game before rerunning this first-launch command.

    On later launches, use the same command without -EvolutionJournal to keep your saved feature selection. Keep using the same save directory.

Do I need a PlayStation BIOS file?

The default build includes OpenBIOS, so the commands above do not require a console BIOS file. Local installer tests have reached the intro, loaded an imported card and entered Pelche Oasis with OpenBIOS. Full battle and save/restart checks remain outstanding.

The more extensively tested backend requires your own matching SCPH-1001 BIOS, supplied to both build and launch commands with -RetailBios 'C:\path\to\bios.bin'. See the BIOS requirements.

Where is the executable?

Inside your Shinka folder: build-windows\Release\dmw2003-shinka.exe. Keep the surrounding build files. For now, use the launch command: it supplies the disc, configuration and save paths. Double-clicking an unconfigured executable can exit before showing a window.

Manual shortcut and saved-path instructions are in the direct-launch guide. The planned installer will create a working shortcut.

03 / Optional

Keep your progress.

Starting fresh? Skip this section. Shinka creates cards in the selected save profile.

To bring a DuckStation save, close DuckStation and Shinka first. Find the game's .mcd memory card in DuckStation's configured memory-card folder. A .sav savestate will not work here.

From the Shinka folder, import into a new profile. Replace the source path with your card's path:

python tools/save_profiles.py import-card 'C:\path\to\your-card.mcd' 'output/imported-save'
./tools/launch_windows.ps1 -DiscCue 'C:\Games\My disc dump\game.cue' -SaveDirectory 'output/imported-save'

The import copies the card and checks the copy. It leaves the original alone and refuses to overwrite an existing destination profile. If that folder already exists, choose a new name. Add your usual BIOS argument if you built with that backend.

In the game, choose Continue and load your save. Keep launching with output/imported-save to use these cards. In-game saves live in card1.mcd and card2.mcd inside that profile.

04 / First session

You're at the title screen.

Start or continue

At language selection, press Start to confirm. Use Start for a new game or Continue for a memory-card save.

Once in the world, open the Start menu. SETTINGS contains EXP, encounters, screen view, soundtrack and battle animation speed. Original music works without an extra music pack; alternate palettes need local music-pack setup.

Controller setup ↗

If something gets stuck

Find the next step.

The window never opens

Use the launch command in the terminal so any error remains visible. Confirm the build finished, the CUE exists, and the BIN it references has not moved. A bare executable does not configure itself yet.

The disc is rejected

Check the release and file format above. The build accepts one specific BIN hash. It will reject another region, a modified dump or a different image layout. Keep the error message; do not bypass the check or rename another format to BIN.

Continue cannot find my save

Check the -SaveDirectory path used for this launch. It should contain your imported card1.mcd. Load through the game's Continue option, not a DuckStation savestate. If you selected a different profile, its cards are separate.

DIGIVOLUTIONS or SETTINGS is missing

Close Shinka, run the first-launch command with -EvolutionJournal, and select English. Reopen menus carried over from an older Shinka savestate.

I moved my disc folder

Update the CUE path in your launch command or configured shortcut. Keep the CUE and BIN together. The current launcher does not have a Locate disc repair screen yet.

In local testing / Not yet released

A guided setup for your own disc.

One guided setup, then a Shinka shortcut. No hand-edited paths, command-line arguments or separate development-tool setup.

  1. Install Shinka

    Install for your Windows account and create a Start-menu shortcut.

  2. Choose your disc dump

    Use a file picker to select your CUE where it already lives. Setup finds the BIN, checks the supported game version and remembers the path. Your original files stay in place.

  3. Prepare the game

    Handle local preparation automatically, with visible progress and a retry option if setup is interrupted.

  4. Bring a save, or start fresh

    Tick Search for existing emulator data to look for DuckStation cards in common locations, or use Choose folder… for a custom setup. Review the cards found and choose one to copy into Shinka. Leave the originals untouched, or skip this step and start fresh.

  5. Play

    Launch from the shortcut next time. If disc files move, offer to locate them again.

The local prototype downloads about 200 MiB of preparation tools and asks for 6 GiB of free space. It builds the game on your computer and keeps your disc files in place. Gameplay, save recovery and clean-PC release checks must pass before a public download appears here.
